content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production services in Java and Spring. Experienced in designing REST APIs, working with relational databases, tuning query performance, and integrating event-driven services with Kafka and RabbitMQ. Hands-on with automated testing, CI/CD, Docker, and deploying services to AWS EKS with Kubernetes. Fluent in English.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech, Lisbon
Jan 2022 – Present
- Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned the REST API for partner quoting integration, used by 12 broker partners and documented with OpenAPI.
- Produce and consume Kafka events in the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, eliminating duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in monthly on-call rotation.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A., Porto
Sep 2019 – Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Helped split the monolith by extracting a notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-time) | CodeFarol Lda, Porto
Jul 2018 – Aug 2019
- Performed PHP and later Java maintenance work for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute, 2018

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java (8–17), Kotlin (basic)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, REST, OpenAPI
Databases and caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis
Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and deployment: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm
Testing and delivery: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Jenkins, CI/CD
Tools: Git, Linux

LANGUAGES
English (fluent) | Portuguese (fluent) | Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and easy to scan. It presents seven years of relevant backend engineering experience with strong quantified impact: reducing p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, increasing test coverage from 35% to 70%, and supporting 12 broker partners. The experience bullets demonstrate production ownership, API design, event-driven architecture, reliability improvements, cloud deployment, and on-call responsibility. The main content limitation is that several job-relevant capabilities appear only in the skills or summary sections rather than being tied to specific work examples. The CV also does not show schema migrations, production incident reviews, observability, or logistics experience, but these are candidate-experience gaps rather than document defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong. The document uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text formatting, recognizable technology names, and no tables, graphics, columns, or parsing-risk elements. It contains strong keyword coverage for Java, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, JUnit, Testcontainers, Jenkins, and CI/CD. AI screening probability is high for a comparable-language backend role, particularly for Java/Spring, REST APIs, relational databases, AWS, Kubernetes, messaging, testing, and CI/CD. Screening probability will be lower for Python/FastAPI-specific searches because neither Python nor FastAPI appears, and the CV does not explicitly state willingness to work mainly in Python. The use of both 'AWS EKS' and 'Kubernetes on AWS EKS' is helpful for keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the comparable-language interpretation of the role. The CV clearly supports seven years of professional Java backend experience, REST API design and consumption, relational database work, query tuning, Docker, AWS deployment, automated testing, CI/CD, Kafka, Kubernetes, EKS, technical documentation, and on-call production ownership. The API versioning and OpenAPI documentation, idempotent consumers, outbox table, latency reduction, and monthly on-call work align well with Tessel's emphasis on dependable services, clear documentation, reliability, and owning what engineers run. The candidate's material does not show Python/FastAPI experience or stated willingness to work mainly in Python. It also does not show schema migrations, observability tooling, Terraform, logistics or EDI knowledge, Dutch or French, blameless post-mortems, or explicit system-design decision notes. These are experience or evidence gaps, not defects that can be solved through rewriting.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Professional Summary, make the comparable-language fit slightly more explicit without claiming Python experience. For example, change the opening to: "Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production backend services in Java and Spring." Keep the existing REST API, relational database, Kafka, testing, CI/CD, Docker, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, and English statements because they closely match the job requirements.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, retain the current concrete examples but make the reliability and production-ownership language more ATS-visible. For example, change "participate in monthly on-call rotation" to "participate in a monthly production on-call rotation" if that accurately reflects the work. Do not add incident response, post-mortems, observability, or design-review claims because they are not present in the original candidate information.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Technical Skills section, keep the current standard category structure and ensure "CI/CD" remains explicitly listed under Testing and delivery, as it is currently supported by the summary and Jenkins pipeline experience. Do not add Python, FastAPI, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, EDI, or logistics terms because they are not supported by the original candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, achievement-focused CV with clear reverse-chronological structure. It communicates relevant backend experience, production ownership, measurable performance improvements, API and event-driven development, testing, deployment, and on-call responsibilities. The bullets are specific and credible, particularly the 1.8-second-to-450-millisecond latency improvement and the increase in test coverage from 35% to 70%. The document is professional and appropriately targeted to a backend engineering role. Minor completeness limitations are the absence of explicit evidence for schema migrations, production incident reviews or post-mortems, technical trade-off communication, and observability tooling; these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional date formatting, simple text-based formatting, and keyword-rich skill categories that should parse reliably in ATS and AI screening systems. Strong matching terms include Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, JUnit, Testcontainers, Jenkins, CI/CD, and on-call. AI screening probability is high for the comparable-language version of the role because the CV clearly demonstrates seven years of Java backend experience and most of the platform requirements. It will be weaker for filters requiring direct Python, FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Terraform, or observability experience, none of which can be added truthfully from the supplied candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the core backend requirements. It shows seven years of professional Java backend development, which is explicitly accepted by the advertisement as a comparable language, plus REST API design, relational databases, query performance work, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, automated testing, CI/CD, Kafka, Kubernetes, and EKS. It also demonstrates production ownership through on-call participation and service deployment. The strongest alignment with the company's reliability culture comes from idempotent consumers, the outbox pattern, latency reduction, duplicate-record prevention, and operating production services. Candidate-material gaps include direct Python/FastAPI experience or an explicit statement of willingness to work mainly in Python, schema migrations, Terraform, Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry, logistics or EDI experience, Dutch/French, and explicit blameless post-mortems. These are gaps in the candidate's supplied background, not defects that can be solved through rewriting.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Professional Summary section, make the comparable-language match even more explicit without claiming Python experience. For example, change the opening to: "Backend engineer with 7 years of professional experience building and operating production backend services in Java and Spring, a comparable language to Python." Keep the existing Kafka, relational database, testing, CI/CD, Docker, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, and English evidence after this sentence.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, change "Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency" to "Improved the public quote REST API's p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds" only if "public" accurately describes the endpoint; otherwise retain the current wording. This more directly connects the quantified achievement to the advertisement's API-performance language without overstating scale.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Technical Skills section, keep the current truthful "Go (side project)" distinction if Go is retained. Do not change it to "2 years of production Go" or imply professional Go experience, because the supplied candidate information says Go was used only in a side project.
